name: core.openwop.workflows.computer-use
description: Computer use (ADR 0418 / ADR 0894). `computer-use.run-task` starts a browser-agent session on the origins you allow, and every commit-class action it wants to take (a submit, a download, a new origin) stops the run and asks you. The approval is the only way a commit proceeds: the decide step raises it itself, so an edited chain cannot remove it.
author: OpenWOP App

chains.label: Computer use: run a browser task
chains.description: Runs a browser agent on a task, inside the origins you list. Reading and on-page input proceed on their own; each submit, download or move to a new origin pauses the run until you approve or reject that one action, and only you can answer. Rejecting, or cancelling the run, ends the session. Needs a browser provider set up by your operator; without one the run stops at the first step and says so. Sites that need you to sign in are not supported yet: the agent never enters credentials, and the run stops with a message when it reaches a sign-in step.

orgId.description: The id of the organization the session belongs to. You need permission to start runs there.

task.description: What the browser agent should do, in plain words.

startUrl.description: The https page to start on. It must be inside the allowed origins.

allowedOrigins.description: The https origins the agent may reach. Anything else ends the session. Private and internal addresses are always refused.

session.description: The session after the last decision: sessionId, status (completed / failed / denied / aborted), steps and any result or error.
